question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$
